feedback.answered: Initial A1/A2 connection: electSelf creates a campaign-local reply channel, advances the term, persists its own vote and requests only latest-configuration voters. runCandidate aggregates that campaign and steps down on a higher-term vote response. Each runLeader constructs a fresh commitment object and replication context; its startIndex is the first index of the new tenure. dispatchLogs assigns current-term indexes, stores locally before reporting its match, and wakes replicators. Successful AppendEntries responses report the last sent entry to that context's commitment object. commitment counts only current configured voters, takes the majority order statistic, and advances only after reaching startIndex. The leader creates a no-op on entry. Thus prior-term persisted history can become committed through current-tenure qualified support rather than carrying an old commitment tracker into the new tenure. Step-down closes replication stop channels and fails inflight/verification futures; the old commitment object is detached. Follower appendEntries rejects lower terms, transitions on newer authority, verifies the predecessor, removes conflicting suffixes, stores replacements, and then advances commit and queues logs toward FSM consumption. Configuration changes are admitted only with a committed latest configuration and a current-term committed entry. These are source observations, not complete applicability or correctness findings. Two retained source questions: (1) follower appendEntries bounds LeaderCommitIndex by its entire local last index while setNewLogs can send only MaxAppendEntries entries; whether a legal leader-generated bounded request can cause consumption of a still-unmatched local suffix needs history analysis. (2) successful DeleteRange followed by failed StoreLogs returns without refreshing cached last-log metadata, explicitly acknowledged by the TODO; whether permitted storage errors allow subsequent participation that consumes that stale metadata remains unresolved.

Read sources for fault assumptions rather than inferring them from error return types.

For the bounded-append question, inspect heartbeat special handling, pipeline request ordering, retry batching, election log freshness and concrete legal divergent-log history before choosing execution; leader current-term commitment threshold is material counterevidence.

For storage-error handling, establish applicable LogStore failure semantics and trace cached last-log consumers, retry paths and possible recovery mechanisms. A synthetically failed store alone would not establish an applicable safety defect.
